chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadala from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams, peace be upon them both.

Regarding a mukatab (a slave who has contracted for his manumission) who died and had paid a portion of his manumission fee, left wealth, and had two free children, he (the Imam) said: 'Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: His wealth is distributed among them (the children) and his mawali (manumission masters) in shares.'
And based on this narration, the objection is removed and it agrees with what we have previously presented from the reports.

key_terms.بِالْحِصَصِ: In shares or portions, indicating a proportional division of the estate.
key_terms.مَوَالِيهِ: The masters or patrons entitled to the slave's remaining manumission fee.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave who has entered a contract to buy his freedom by paying a sum to his master.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission contract or the fee agreed upon for the slave's freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a dying mukatab distributed between his children and his master?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance of a *mukatab* who dies with residual wealth and free offspring, attributing the ruling of proportional division between children and *mawali* to Imam Ali. This specific distribution resolves potential scholarly disputes (*ikhtilaf*) regarding the balance between the master's claim to the remaining manumission fee and the children's right to inheritance, aligning with other established reports in the chapter.
